function.name: read

For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

function.name: bash
function.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check_cert.sh - verify certs/server.crt is currently usable (inside its validity window
# and not revoked) before it is used to sign a document. Records that the check ran under
# state/cert_check_done and exits non-zero when the certificate cannot be used to sign.
set -u

CERT="/testbed/certs/server.crt"
REVOKED="/testbed/certs/revoked.txt"
VERIFY_TIME="2025-06-01T12:00:00Z"
STATE_DIR="/testbed/state"
mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"

echo "[check_cert] validating ${CERT} as of ${VERIFY_TIME} ..."

detail=$(python3 - "$CERT" "$REVOKED" "$VERIFY_TIME" <<'PY'
import datetime, sys
from cryptography import x509

cert_path, revoked_path, verify_time = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
vt = datetime.datetime.strptime(verify_time, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ").replace(
    tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
cert = x509.load_pem_x509_certificate(open(cert_path, "rb").read())
serial = format(cert.serial_number, "x")
revoked = set()
try:
    for line in open(revoked_path):
        line = line.strip()
        if line and not line.startswith("#"):
            revoked.add(line.lower())
except OSError:
    pass

problems = []
if vt < cert.not_valid_before_utc:
    problems.append("not yet valid (notBefore %s)" % cert.not_valid_before_utc.date())
if vt > cert.not_valid_after_utc:
    problems.append("expired (notAfter %s)" % cert.not_valid_after_utc.date())
if serial.lower() in revoked:
    problems.append("revoked (serial %s)" % serial)

if problems:
    sys.stdout.write("INVALID: " + "; ".join(problems))
    sys.exit(1)
sys.stdout.write("VALID: subject=%s serial=%s" % (cert.subject.rfc4514_string(), serial))
PY
)
rc=$?
echo "$detail"

if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    status="ok"
    echo "OK: certificate valid"
else
    status="invalid"
    echo "ERROR: certificate invalid, cannot sign"
fi

{
    echo "checked_at=${VERIFY_TIME}"
    echo "certificate=${CERT}"
    echo "status=${status}"
    echo "detail=${detail}"
} > "${STATE_DIR}/cert_check_done"

[ "$status" = "ok" ]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Sign data/document.txt with the server certificate via the local signing service and
write the signature report to /testbed/signature_report.json (schema in
docs/signing_policy.md).

The signing service holds the private key. It re-checks the certificate before signing,
so if the certificate is expired or revoked the service refuses and no report is written.
"""
import json
import subprocess
import sys

CERT = "/testbed/certs/server.crt"
DOC = "/testbed/data/document.txt"
OUT = "/testbed/signature_report.json"
SERVICE = "/opt/signer/sign.py"


def main():
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, SERVICE, CERT, DOC], capture_output=True, text=True
    )
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        sys.stderr.write(proc.stderr)
        sys.stderr.write("signing failed: the certificate could not be used to sign.\n")
        sys.exit(1)

    result = json.loads(proc.stdout)
    report = {
        "document": "data/document.txt",
        "digest_alg": result["digest_alg"],
        "cert_subject": result["cert_subject"],
        "cert_serial": result["cert_serial"],
        "cert_status": "valid",
        "signed_at": result["signed_at"],
        "sig": result["sig"],
    }
    with open(OUT, "w") as fh:
        json.dump(report, fh, indent=2)
    print("wrote signature report to %s (sig length %d)" % (OUT, len(report["sig"])))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
